title: Phasecraft Establishes U.S. Headquarters in Arlington, Virginia to Accelerate Government and Defense Quantum Software Partnerships - Quantum Computing Report
gist: UK-rooted quantum software firm Phasecraft has established its official US headquarters in Ballston, Arlington County, Virginia, backed by the Virginia Economic Development Partnership and Virginia Jobs Investment Program funding. The move follows its selection into DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative and an ARPA-E computational chemistry program, positioning the company as a federal defense and energy contractor rather than a pure commercial software vendor.

insights.claim: Phasecraft has selected Ballston in Arlington County, Virginia as its official United States headquarters, placing its operational base inside the Washington DC metropolitan area to sit alongside federal stakeholders and defense-tech ecosystems.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Physical siting next to agency buyers signals the revenue model is government contracts, not enterprise SaaS — value accrues on budget cycles, not sales cycles.
insights.quote: Phasecraft has selected Arlington County, Virginia (Ballston) as the location for its official United States headquarters.
insights.locator: Quantum software company Phasecraft has selected

insights.claim: The US expansion is supported by the Virginia Economic Development Partnership and state funding through the Virginia Jobs Investment Program, meaning part of the workforce build-out cost is subsidised by state incentives rather than investor capital.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: State-level incentive competition for quantum firms is now material to siting decisions; watch which states escalate packages next.
insights.locator: Supported by the Virginia Economic Development Partnership

insights.claim: Earlier in 2026 Phasecraft joined DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative to provide verification, validation and benchmarking of fault-tolerant algorithm utility, placing it in the referee role rather than competing as a hardware builder.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Benchmarking mandates give unusual visibility into rival hardware roadmaps and make the firm a bellwether for which quantum platforms clear DARPA screens.
insights.quote: Earlier in 2026, the company joined the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency’s (DARPA) Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) program to provide verification, validation, and benchmarking of fault-tolerant algorithm utility.
insights.locator: The U.S. expansion builds on Phasecraft’s growing engagements

insights.claim: ARPA-E selected Phasecraft under its Quantum Computing for Computational Chemistry program to engineer optimized quantum algorithms for simulating advanced catalytic materials, tying quantum software revenue to the energy-materials discovery budget line.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Catalyst simulation is the nearest-term credible quantum use case; federal funding here is the leading indicator of commercial chemistry adoption.
insights.locator: Additionally, Phasecraft was selected by the Advanced Research Projects Agency–Energy

insights.claim: Phasecraft's stated sector span is defense, energy and materials science simultaneously, which for a company of this stage implies revenue concentrated in a handful of agency programs rather than a diversified commercial book.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Program-renewal risk dominates; a single non-renewal at DARPA or ARPA-E would be outsized news for the company.
insights.locator: [ Phasecraft U.S. Expansion & Federal Program Footprint ]

insights.claim: Phasecraft's proprietary algorithms are optimized to minimize gate depth and qubit overheads for near-term and early fault-tolerant quantum processors, a software-efficiency strategy that extracts value from whatever hardware wins rather than betting on a single modality.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hardware-agnostic algorithm layers are the lower-capex way to own quantum exposure; they benefit from qubit scarcity instead of being punished by it.
insights.quote: optimized to minimize gate depth and qubit overheads for near-term and early fault-tolerant quantum processors
